# Case sheets

Readable clinical case files for development, generated from the playable registry by `scripts/case-sheets.ts`. Do not edit them by hand:

- `npm run cases` regenerates them after you change a case, a map or the catalog.
- `npm run cases:check` exits non-zero when they are stale; `npm test` runs the same check.

Every case can be played individually or drawn in a mixed shift. Each sheet includes its provenance, hidden truth, history, exam, physiology, investigations, scoring and teaching. Fixed shift assignments are in [maps.md](maps.md).

| [**Acute uncomplicated cystitis**](uncomplicated_cystitis.md)<br>`uncomplicated_cystitis` · 27 F · Frequent painful urination | Acute uncomplicated cystitis (N30.00) | 4 | Assigned at arrival | • Dysuria and frequency without vaginal or systemic symptoms support a lower urinary infection<br>• Check pregnancy possibility and factors that make the infection complicated before selecting oral treatment<br>• Choose the regimen and duration using local resistance guidance… |
| [**Acute uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulitis**](uncomplicated_diverticulitis.md)<br>`uncomplicated_diverticulitis` · 59 M · Left lower abdominal ache | Acute uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulitis (K57.32) | 3 | Assigned at arrival | • This patient is systemically well, drinking and has no CT complication<br>• Selective antibiotic use is reasonable in uncomplicated disease…<br>• Outpatient care requires clear deterioration advice and accessible reassessment |
| [**Urosepsis (pyelonephritis) in a delirious older adult with prior ESBL E. coli**](urosepsis_esbl.md)<br>`urosepsis_esbl` · 81 F · Confusion, weakness | Sepsis due to acute pyelonephritis (prior ESBL E. coli), with acute kidney injury and delirium (A41.51 / R65.20 / N10 / N17.9 / F05 / Z16.12) | 2 | [Night Shift](maps.md#night-shift): Bed 4, 22:04 (+4 min) | • Sepsis = infection + organ dysfunction (ΔSOFA ≥ 2)<br>• Hour-1 bundle: lactate, blood cultures BEFORE antibiotics, broad-spectrum antibiotics…<br>• Prior microbiology matters: with prior ESBL E. coli, ceftriaxone is likely inadequate…<br>• Check triage vitals for completeness — a missing temperature hides a SIRS criterion and a sepsis screen<br>• Delirium is a medical emergency; establish baseline cognition with collateral history<br>• Low-risk penicillin allergy labels rarely preclude cephalosporins or carbapenems |

| [**Vasovagal syncope**](vasovagal_syncope.md)<br>`vasovagal_syncope` · 23 F · Fainted while watching a blood draw | Vasovagal syncope (R55) | 3 | Assigned at arrival | • A witnessed trigger, autonomic prodrome and rapid complete recovery support reflex syncope<br>• History, examination and ECG must still screen for a cardiac cause<br>• Avoid routine brain imaging in a clear uncomplicated faint without neurologic or trauma indications |

| [**Acute viral pharyngitis**](viral_pharyngitis.md)<br>`viral_pharyngitis` · 21 F · Sore throat, runny nose and hoarseness | Acute viral pharyngitis (J02.9) | 5 | Assigned at arrival | • Hoarseness, cough and coryza favor a viral cause<br>• Cough, coryza and hoarseness make a viral syndrome more likely; check for airway or deep-neck warning signs<br>• For this mild presentation, symptom care and expectations matter more than investigations<br>• Explain what changes would require reassessment rather than giving an unsupported antibiotic prescription |
| [**Exertional heat exhaustion**](warm_race_finish.md)<br>`warm_race_finish` · 31 M · Cramps and dizziness at the finish line | Exertional heat exhaustion (T67.5XXA) | 3 | Assigned at arrival | • Check mentation and temperature to distinguish heat exhaustion from heat stroke<br>• Altered mental status raises concern for heat stroke even if a later temperature is lower after cooling<br>• The scripted falling temperature assumes the already documented removal from heat |
